server.instructions:
CandleStack is a lab for experiments on financial time series: a user uploads a trading model (Keras or ONNX), describes its input in a manifest and backtests it on market data, crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca, then compares the results and publishes the good ones.

You act as the user whose API key signed in. The key's scopes decide which tools work: read (everything that only reads), backtests, models and publish. Call get_me first to see who you act for and what the key may do. A tool that changes data says so in its annotations.

A failed tool call answers a problem as JSON: its type (https://candlestack.tech/problems/<slug>) names what went wrong and its detail says what to do.

Docs for agents: https://candlestack.tech/docs/agents/ and for this server: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/. The resource candlestack://docs lists every docs page and reference.

tools.description:
Who you act for: the CandleStack user whose API key signed in, and the key's scopes, which decide the tools you may call. Call it first to check the connection, and when a tool answers the problem missing-scope.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#get_me
tools.name: get_me

Scope.description:
What an API key may do. `read`: every GET; `backtests`: start, rename and star
backtests; `models`: upload models, add their manifests, rename, star and delete them;
`publish`: publish and unpublish backtests. Managing keys, deleting the account, sign-in
methods and signing out need the browser session whatever the scopes.
